The Growth Accounting Framework Growth accounting is like maintaining a detailed health record for your business or product. For example, if you are tracking app usage, growth accounting helps you understand exactly where users originate and where they navigate within the app. It’s similar to reviewing your bank statement to monitor money coming in and going out, except here, you are tracking user activity. Growth accounting helps you in three primary ways: · It helps you understand what’s really driving your growth: whether it’s new users signing up, existing users staying active, or former users coming back. · It alerts you to potential problems early: whether too many users are leaving (churning) or you are not attracting enough new users. · It helps you make better decisions about where to focus your efforts for driving growth: whether that’s improving user retention, acquiring new users, or reengaging lost users. Understanding User Growth: An Introduction to Growth Accounting Every product has users, and tracking their growth is essential. User growth accounting helps understand how users interact with a product over time by doing the following: · Analyze user engagement history. · Measure the impact of new user acquisition. · Track retention and churn rates. The growth accounting framework provides crucial insights into a company’s growth. In this chapter, we’ll first explore this framework in detail, and explore other growth accounting methods later in the chapter. Creating a Growth Accounting Framework Core Components A growth accounting framework comprises four essential elements: 1. Unit This is the fundamental element you track, typically aligned with your North Star metric. For example, in Monthly Active Users (MAU), one unit represents one user. 2. Active Status Clearly define what makes a unit “active.” This should reflect meaningful engagement with your product. For example: · Video app: Watching content for at least ten seconds · Chat app: Successfully sending a message 3. Time Granularity Choose how often you’ll measure user activity (daily, weekly, monthly). This choice should align with your desired user engagement frequency. 4. State Transitions Monitor how units move between active and inactive status. The five main statuses are: · New: First-time users · Retained: Users active yesterday and today · Churned: Users active yesterday who are inactive today · Resurrected: Users inactive yesterday who became active today (not first-time) · Stale: Users inactive both yesterday and today Note: These states can be measured at daily, weekly, or monthly intervals. {YuzhengSun Graphic18} Figure 3-1: Growth accounting states Fundamental User Growth Accounting Metrics Growth accounting metrics are derived by combining different states into meaningful calculations that inform product strategy. Two key metrics that emerge from these combinations are: 1. xAU = New + Resurrected + Retained, where x is the abbreviation of time granularity 2. Net growth = New + Resurrected – Churned Users These metrics are explained in the following sections: xAU When using the xAU metric, if we’re measuring Daily Active Users (DAU), the x would be D for daily. Similarly, WAU represents Weekly Active Users, and MAU represents Monthly Active Users. This formula helps you to understand the composition of your active user base at any given time interval. As shown in Figure 3-1, different transition states can be used to calculate the volume of your business units in active and inactive status. For example, Daily Active Users can be decomposed as follows: DAU = D1 New + D1 Resurrected + D1 Retained where D1 New = Users who were new to the product today D1 Resurrected = Users who resurrected for today D1 Retained = Users who were in retained status for today A general equation for active users is xAU = Dx New + Dx Resurrected + Dx Retained. In this equation, x represents the unit of time used to measure the active users, which can be daily, weekly, bi-weekly, monthly, or any other specified interval. Net Growth Net growth measures how many users you are growing/shrinking compared to yesterday. DAUnet growth = D1 New + D1 Resurrected – D1 Churned where D1 New = Users who were new to the product today D1 Resurrected = Users who resurrected for today D1 Churned = Users who were in churned status for today Successful products should demonstrate consistent growth. This means that your net growth—the number of users you gained minus those lost—should be positive whether measured daily, weekly, or monthly. However, it’s important to recognize that positive net growth does not always indicate sustainable success. It can sometimes conceal underlying issues. For example, positive growth might occur simply because you invest heavily into acquiring new users (the “new” component), while existing users are leaving at an alarming rate. Understanding Transitions To track these patterns accurately, compare user activity between two time periods: a previous window and a current window. It’s like taking two snapshots of your user base and analyzing the differences. For instance, we classify a user as “resurrected” if they were inactive in the previous window but become active in the current window. Nonoverlapping windows may seem like a logical approach. For example, one might assume monthly churn involves counting users who were active last month but inactive this month. However, this method does not accurately calculate churn in growth accounting. {YuzhengSun Graphic19} Figure 3-2: Nonoverlapping window illustration Instead, growth accounting uses overlapping windows to accurately track user transitions. For example, when calculating monthly churn on January 31: · Previous window: January 1–30 · Current window: January 2–31 {YuzhengSun Graphic20{ Figure 3-3: Overlapping window illustration The overlapping approach captures daily changes in user behavior and aligns with the net growth equation. It provides a more accurate picture of user transitions by accounting for users who may be active at different points within the month, rather than just comparing two separate months. Let’s see how this works in practice. Remember that MAU net growth (MAU today – MAU yesterday) = MAU new + MAU resurrected – MAU churned. Since this calculation measures daily changes in MAU, applying overlapping windows ensures accuracy. Here’s a practical example showing how to calculate MAU growth accounting states as of January 31, demonstrating the specific dates used for previous and current windows: Case Study Let’s examine a case study of MGA, a mobile gaming application that launched six months ago and is now focusing on growth. Key Framework Parameters · Unit of analysis: Individual users · Active user definition: Users who spend more than ten seconds playing a game · Time granularity: Monthly Active Users (MAU) as the North Star metric Growth Analysis: January Performance Review MAU Trend MAU has grown significantly—up approximately 52 percent each week and quadrupling over the month. This represents strong growth. Let’s decompose the MAU metric to understand which states have been driving this growth and what opportunities exist for further expansion. {YuzhengSun Graphic21} Figure 3-4: MAU trend The following chart shows the breakdown of the MAU trend by different growth accounting buckets. {YuzhengSun Graphic22} Figure 3-5: Detailed component trend analysis 1. New User Acquisition {YuzhengSun Graphic23} Figure 3-6: New user acquisition trend · Notable dip on January 10. · Initial slowdown in first two weeks. · Significant acceleration post-January 21, coinciding with a new marketing campaign. 2. Churned User {YuzhengSun Graphic24} Figure 3-7: Churned user trend · Elevated rates observed in late January. · No correlation with seasonal events or holidays. · Requires further investigation into root causes. 3. Resurrected User {YuzhengSun Graphic25} Figure 3-8: Resurrected user trend · Major spike recorded on January 28. · Success attributed to targeted notification strategy and marketing initiatives. 4. Retained User {YuzhengSun Graphic26} Figure 3-9: Retained user trend · Initial plateau in mid-January. · Strong acceleration in latter half of month. · Overall positive trend indicating healthy user engagement. After analyzing growth trends, the next question becomes which growth accounting category to prioritize to drive growth. While trend analysis provides valuable insights, the critical step involves developing and testing hypotheses about the causes of these trends and determining which hypotheses are feasible to pursue. New users: New users grew 73 percent week-over-week (WoW) and doubled over the month. Analyzing the different market segments within the total addressable market for mobile gaming reveals that teens in Japan represent a promising market for user acquisition. Ads through Google and Meta launched on January 16, increasing awareness and downloads of the gaming app. After confirming these cohorts demonstrate strong retention, campaign spending can increase to acquire more users. {YuzhengSun Graphic27} Figure 3-10: New user growth rate Retained users: Retained users grew 62 percent WoW and sixfold over the month. If retained users occasionally trend down intermittently, it may indicate increasing churn over time. The app shows that retained users remained flat or trended down during specific periods. To ensure continuous growth in this metric, focus on enhancing user retention and engagement among retained users. {YuzhengSun Graphic28} Figure 3-11: Retained user growth rate Resurrected users: User resurrection increased by 251 percent week-over-week and nearly doubled over the month. The significant growth in resurrection last week resulted from a major spike on January 28, following the launch of new language translation features for Japanese teens. Notifications sent to this audience contributed to the spike. {YuzhengSun Graphic29} Figure 3-12: Resurrected user growth rate Churned users: To assess how bad churn is, we often look at net growth to begin with. How is churn affecting my growth? To understand the effect of churn, first examine net growth to determine whether it has been negative. Remember, net growth measures the change in the number of users compared to yesterday. {YuzhengSun Graphic30} Figure 3-13: Net growth trend Net growth consistently showed negative trends since mid-January but increased significantly during the last few days of the month. Now is the time to analyze the components of net growth to understand the impact of churn. {YuzhengSun Graphic31} Figure 3-14: Trend of net growth components Resurrections were significantly lower between January 15 to January 20 compared to churn, resulting in negative net growth. Churn rates also increased after January 23, primarily because the app lacked sufficient language support for Japanese users. As a result, many Japanese youth acquired during mid-January began to churn. However, following the launch of Japanese language support, many of the churned users resurrected on January 28. Growth Accounting Framework Variations Variation 1: Business Growth Accounting Traditional growth accounting primarily emphasizes active user metrics. However, an important variation applies this framework to revenue analysis. This approach enables businesses to understand the financial impact of user behavior patterns. See Chapter 7 for a detailed discussion. Variation 2: Specialized Growth State Segmentation Organic vs. Inorganic User Transitions As products scale, they attract both legitimate users and potential bad actors, making it essential to distinguish between organic and inorganic user transitions. Inorganic churn occurs when users are deactivated due to: · Detection of suspicious activity · Identification of bot accounts · Violations of policy Monitoring inorganic churn is crucial for mature products to develop effective defense strategies. Users may temporarily enter an inorganic churn state while under investigation. If cleared, they transition to inorganic resurrection, which helps track false positive rates in integrity systems. Voluntary vs. Nonvoluntary Churn in SaaS In Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) businesses, understanding churn patterns requires distinguishing between voluntary decisions. Voluntary churn occurs when users actively choose to leave, such as a Netflix subscriber canceling due to perceived low value. Nonvoluntary churn may result from circumstances like: · Payment processing failures · Policy-related account suspensions · Technical access issues This distinction informs mitigation strategies: address voluntary churn with product improvements, and address nonvoluntary churn with operational solutions like better payment systems. Variation 3: Enhanced State Definitions Growth accounting frameworks can be customized with additional granularity in active/inactive state definitions. When considering such modifications, ask: “How will granular status distinctions impact business decisions and actions?” Duolingo exemplifies this approach by incorporating “at risk” states into its user classification system. Their framework distinguishes between Weekly Active Users (WAU) and Monthly Active Users (MAU) at risk of churning, which enables targeted engagement strategies. {YuzhengSun Graphic32} Figure 3-15: Duolingo growth model This granular approach allows Duolingo to implement specific gamification strategies for different user risk categories, demonstrating how enhanced state definitions can drive targeted intervention strategies. Takeaway Growth accounting serves as a powerful framework that breaks down user growth into its core components, providing a comprehensive view of your product’s health and growth dynamics. By analyzing user transitions between different statuses—from new to retained, churned to resurrected—you can identify the key drivers of your product’s growth and areas needing attention. To implement an effective growth accounting framework: 1. Define meaningful activity metrics that reflect genuine user value. 2. Map distinct user states and their transition status. 3. Systematically track state transitions. 4. Focus on the states that most significantly impact net growth. The power of growth accounting lies in its ability to: · Guide strategic decisions by revealing which user segments require attention, whether it’s acquiring new users, retaining existing ones, or reengaging churned users. · Provide actionable insights through historical trend analysis, enabling teams to evaluate the effectiveness of past initiatives and identify emerging challenges. · Enable competitive benchmarking through standardized metrics like churn and resurrection rates. · Offer a holistic view of product health that extends beyond individual metrics, ensuring balanced and sustainable growth. --- Chapter 10: Design and Implement Effective Experiments⁠ The Role of Experimentation in Product Growth Experimentation Moves the Team from Insights to Action In the previous chapters, you learned how to identify growth opportunities through a deep dive into your data. You pinpointed areas where your product shines and where optimization is feasible. However, identifying these opportunities is just the beginning. To drive effective growth with confidence and ensure team alignment, validate your hypotheses with solid evidence. This is where experimentation, particularly A/B testing, is essential, enabling you to transition from insights to action. All Useful Analyses Are Causal Analyses You may wonder, What about prediction models, growth accounting, or funnel analysis? Aren’t those focused on correlations, rather than causation? While this is true, your primary responsibility as a data analyst or a data scientist is to establish clear causal claims. You must be able to assert, “Based on my analysis, I recommend pursuing A instead of B, because I believe A will attract more users, boost engagement, or increase revenue.” Essentially, you are saying, “This change will cause that outcome.” Thus, all valuable analyses should aim to demonstrate a causal relationship. When strong causal evidence exists, the path forward is clear. If not, it’s your responsibility to build a convincing argument that your recommendation will positively impact the business. Data can be highly persuasive, but only when presented clearly and supported by sound reasoning. This is why experimentation—specifically randomized controlled trials, the gold standard of A/B testing—is crucial for product growth. These experiments provide the strongest possible evidence to support your decisions. While other ways to gather insights exist, make experiments your default approach whenever possible. A Quick Introduction to Randomized Control Trials and Causal Inference {YuzhengSun Graphic54} Figure 10-1: The Evidence Pyramid (Source: “The Evidence Pyriamid,” University of New England, accessed July 8, 2025, https://library.une.edu/research-help/help-with/evidence-based-practice/the-evidence-pyramid/). The evidence pyramid ranks types of studies according to their strength and reliability. At the pinnacle are randomized controlled trials (RCTs), considered the most rigorous form of unfiltered evidence. Results from well-conducted A/B tests should take precedence over other forms of evidence due to their high reliability. Consider the following example. You want to change the messaging on a call-to-action (CTA) button from “Purchase” to “Buy Now” with the aim of boosting conversion rates. Here’s a step-by-step application of the evidence pyramid: 1. Expert opinions: Consult professionals to determine whether this change is likely to be effective. 2. Case studies: Review case studies or other businesses that implemented similar changes to their CTA buttons. 3. Data analysis: Systematically analyze data to identify patterns comparing buttons labeled “Purchase” and “Buy Now.” 4. Cohort studies: Implement the change from the “Purchase” button to “Buy Now,” then monitor conversion rates before and after the change. 5. Randomized controlled trial (RCT): Randomly assign half the users to see the “Purchase” button, while the other half observes the “Buy Now” button. Compare the conversion rates between these two groups. By following these steps, you can ensure that your decision-making process is grounded in the strongest available evidence. Each step builds on the previous one by addressing potential biases: 1. Transition from expert opinion to case studies: Experts can be wrong or biased, so seek patterns in real-world cases to inform decisions. 2. Transition from case studies to systematic comparisons: Because case studies may not be relevant to your customers or your circumstances, conduct comparisons to gain broader insights. 3. Transition from comparisons to cohort studies: Comparisons alone cannot determine whether changes in outcomes result from the intervention or from other factors, such as seasonality or external events. 4. Transition from cohort studies to RCTs: Only RCTs, such as A/B testing, can adequately control for all variables. With random assignment, you can confidently attribute differences between groups to the treatment—in this case, changing “Purchase” to “Buy Now.” The effectiveness of A/B testing lies in two key principles: 1. Random assignment: By randomly assigning one group to experience the change (button “Buy Now”) and another to remain unchanged (button “Purchase”), any differences in results (such as age, income, height, and conversion rate on your call to action) can be attributed to the treatment rather than external factors or chance. 2. The law of large numbers: When a sufficiently large sample size is randomly split into two groups, their average traits (e.g., age, income, height, and conversion rate on your call to action) will be statistically similar. A/B testing offers exceptional value because it requires no additional assumptions beyond following proper procedures. Conduct rigorous tests to obtain the most reliable evidence possible. If A/B testing is an option, use it—it’s the gold standard for making evidence-based decisions. Key Factors for Successful Experimentation Successful product growth teams excel at the 80/20 rule, recognizing that 20 percent of their efforts can yield 80 percent of the results. The focus remains on the vital few rather than the trivial many. This principle applies to experimentation as well. Consider the following critical elements: - Clear hypothesis: Define what you are testing and why. - Solid infrastructure: - Balanced groups: Ensure test and control groups are truly comparable. - Accurate logging: Track relevant data accurately and effectively. - Easy setup: Create tests quickly and effortlessly. - Comprehensive metrics: Monitor a wide range of metrics efficiently. - Culture of experimentation: - Openness to ideas: Empower every team member to suggest experiments. - Collaborative decisions: Foster a team-based approach to decision-making rather than top-down directives. - Humility: Accept that most initial ideas may not produce the expected outcomes. - Celebrate learning: Emphasize lessons learned from each experiment, regardless of whether the outcome is a “success” or a “failure.” - Iterative development: Continuously refine the product based on experimental results. Avoid getting bogged down in the intricate statistical details, which are important but warrant a separate discussion, such as in the book Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments . This chapter focuses on the big picture: what scalable experimentation entails and why it serves as a game-changer for product growth. To grasp the importance of experiments, first recognize how often initial ideas miss the mark. Embrace Being Wrong: Why Most Ideas Initially Fail A significant gap exists in how people perceive their own ideas. Those who run experiments regularly understand the value of humility regarding their initial hypotheses because they witness how often they fall short. Research indicates that around 80 percent of initial ideas fail to deliver the expected results, across various companies and teams.[[1]]( ftn1) In contrast, individuals who seldom experiment typically overestimate the success rates of their ideas. Accepting this reality can be challenging. To understand why this is the case, consider the following two main reasons: 1. Tackling difficult problems: If ideas succeeded most of the time, it would mean that we’re dealing with simpler issues. However, product growth operates at the forefront of product development, marketing, and industry best practices. There are no guarantees that any idea will work perfectly on the first attempt. 2. Complexity of modern products: The ecosystem surrounding today’s products is extraordinarily intricate. This complexity overwhelms the human brain’s capacity to fully comprehend every aspect simultaneously. The first point is intuitive, while the second one is more nuanced. To illustrate this complexity, consider the story of DDT and bald eagles as an analogy. {YuzhengSun Graphic55} Figure 10-2: DDT and bald eagles statistics In the 1940s, scientists celebrated DDT as a breakthrough pesticide, impressed by its remarkable effectiveness and concluding, after extensive research, that it posed no significant environmental risk. However, the consequences emerged years later. Bald eagles were indirectly harmed by DDT after consuming contaminated fish. As the pesticide moved up the food chain, it became increasingly concentrated, weakening eagle eggshells. This fragility caused eggs to break easily during incubation, leading to a sharp decline in the eagle population. Looking back, the connection seems obvious, but no one at the time could have foreseen the complex ripple effects triggered by DDT. Modern products often face similarly intricate challenges: markets are diverse, user needs vary widely, and products themselves can be extraordinarily complex. Acknowledging this reality requires humility in how we approach predictions and an understanding that outcomes may differ significantly from expectations. Once you accept these realities, the necessity of experimentation for achieving sustainable, compounding growth becomes clear. Understanding what works, what does not, and how to make improvements is essential for success. {YuzhengSun Graphic56} Figure 10-3: Mistaking motion with progress To better internalize the ideas behind experimentation, consider the following real-life examples. Example One: Shifting the Priority of Marketplace Product with A/B Testing My conviction about A/B testing solidified during an attempt to promote e-commerce on a marketplace product within a social app during the COVID-19 pandemic. We initially failed, but through a pivot, we eventually achieved success. A/B Testing Revealed the Failure Marketplace seemed like a natural fit for e-commerce since users frequently shopped there. Our product leader came from eBay, and we recruited teams from companies like Walmart. These teams entered war rooms to create an e-commerce-first experience on Marketplace. Coming from Amazon, I was excited about the initiative and willingly worked many overnight shifts. The first major launch on the main tab featured a well-thought-out design with a modern aesthetic, seamless checkout flow, and dedicated teams curating attractive and relevant selections. We also matched competitors’ prices with subsidies and offered generous return policies. Fortunately, we conducted an A/B test for the launch, which revealed a disastrous outcome. The result shocked everyone, including me. The test revealed declines in nearly every metric: conversion rates from the product detail page to checkout, click-through rates from browse to the product detail page, the number of browse impressions, and Daily Active Users. It was clear: Marketplace users hated what we launched . When a failure occurs, two primary reasons typically emerge: either the concept is flawed, or the execution of the idea fails. Naturally, leaders questioned the execution—and justifiably so. I questioned our execution as well. Analyzing the Failure Through Experiments Fortunately, another experiment helped the team avoid pursuing a doomed idea and facing repercussions for its failure. The experiment was designed to provide strong evidence that e-commerce simply does not work on Marketplace. Our hypothesis suggested that Marketplace users are specifically seeking deals; they are just not generally interested in e-commerce products. In hindsight, this makes sense: Why would users buy an e-commerce product from a social app when they can rely on Amazon? However, how could we convince those determined to make e-commerce successful on our platform? The Impact of a White Background We discovered that most “Marketplace native” products feature in-context backgrounds with their product images—like displaying an item on a table—while most e-commerce products use plain, professional white backgrounds. To test this, we randomized the backgrounds of a consistent set of products, displaying either a white background image or an in-context image on the browse feed. Our findings showed that the white background led to decreases in both click-through and conversion rates: users felt as if they were in a traditional e-commerce experience rather than browsing for deals. {YuzhengSun Graphic57} Figure 10-4: The two variants: Which one feels more like an e-commerce experience? The Impact of A/B Testing The significance of A/B testing resonated deeply with me. Before the white background experiment, I endured countless meetings filled with debates over which ideas would succeed, who was responsible for poor executions, and how to improve our processes. After the white background experiment, those debates quickly concluded. We redirected our efforts toward enabling shipping for Marketplace local listings and achieved a twenty-six-time increase in online transactions on Marketplace over the next six months—outperforming similar social shopping apps combined. Without these two experiments, many people’s careers or lives would have been negatively affected. At times, it feels as if leaders become villains in these narratives: poor strategy, misguided decisions, a lack of understanding of the business, and shifting blame to direct reports. However, upon conducting an honest postmortem, I realized my perspective shifted midway through the journey. It’s challenging to recognize reality when you are fully immersed in making an idea work. To me, that’s the true power of causal evidence and A/B testing: I believe even Mark Zuckerberg himself could not have convinced me more effectively. Example Two: Can Lower-Quality Video Increase Revenue? Vijaye Raji, former VP and Head of Entertainment at Facebook, shared an intriguing story about how a seemingly negative change in video quality yielded unexpectedly positive results. This experience emphasized the critical role of experimentation and challenging assumptions in product development. The COVID-19 Challenge During the COVID-19 pandemic, people turned to video for entertainment and connection, which significantly increased internet usage. This surge strained internet infrastructure and threatened essential online services. Governments and telecommunication companies urged video platforms to reduce bandwidth consumption. The Counterintuitive Solution In response, an engineering team, led by Vijaye, decided to experiment with reducing video quality to decrease bandwidth usage. Their goal was to quantify the impact of reduced video quality on watch time and ad revenue. They anticipated a decline, as the organization had heavily invested in the belief that users prefer higher-quality videos. Past experiments consistently showed that better video quality led to increased watch time and ad revenue. The Surprising Results To their astonishment, the experiment yielded unexpected results. Although bandwidth usage decreased as intended, both watch time and ad revenue increased instead of declining. This counterintuitive outcome prompted further investigation. Had the entire organization been wrong all along? What about all the engineering and hardware resources invested in enhancing video quality? The Root Cause In some organizations, leadership may choose to ignore negative results or bury them. Fortunately, Vijaye prioritized uncovering the truth. He assembled a dedicated data science team to investigate. By meticulously analyzing experiment results and comparing them with other analytics, the team quickly identified the root cause. They discovered that during the pandemic, users, particularly in developing countries like India, faced usage quotas set by their carriers. By watching lower-quality videos, users could consume more content, which ultimately led to increased overall watch time and ad revenue. The Power of Experimentation In hindsight, could engineers have anticipated the impact of usage quotas? It’s a challenging task. Similar to the insights gained from the bald eagle and DDT story, it’s impossible for anyone to foresee every variable. This is why experimentation is essential. However, the value of successful experimentation must be rooted in a truth-seeking culture. I hope this story serves as a reminder that experimentation can uncover unexpected insights and drive product growth, especially in dynamic situations. A Deep Dive into Scalable Experimentation What Is Scalable Experimentation? Scalable experimentation involves making experimentation the default practice rather than the exception. Modern software development techniques, particularly feature flags and CI/CD (continuous integration/continuous delivery), have made this approach not only feasible but also optimal. Consider the following: with feature flags, you can control when and to whom a new feature is released. This allows you to separate the act of deploying code from the process of changing a feature’s configuration or visibility. This separation is a fundamental principle of modern software development. With feature flags in place, you already have the foundation for scalable experiments. You have complete control over which users experience different versions of your product. By incorporating randomization, you create a system where experimentation becomes the norm rather than an isolated event. We’ve identified seven key criteria for a scalable experimentation infrastructure. Use these to assess your own system: 1. Define metrics once and use them everywhere: Eliminate the need to reinvent the wheel for each experiment. 2. Ensure reliable and transparent data: Establish clarity so everyone understands the data’s meaning and origin. 3. Build, test, and deploy the same code: Reduce the risk of introducing errors when launching experiments. 4. Foster a culture of experimentation: Make experimentation an integral part of your team’s DNA (refer to the “Best Practices for Building an Experimentation Culture” section that follows). 5. Provide clear, layered information: Present data in an easily understandable format to support informed decision-making. 6. Utilize a trustworthy and practical statistical engine: Avoid overly complex statistical methods that are difficult to interpret. 7. Automate wherever possible: Streamline the process by automating logging, health checks, calculations, experiment management, and any other tasks. {YuzhengSun Graphic58} {YuzhengSun Graphic59} Figure 10-5: How to have default-on experimentation Why Is Scalable Experimentation Necessary? Experiments are incredibly valuable, but they’re not “necessary” in the same way that using Excel for basic accounting is. Experiments focus on discovering new growth opportunities rather than maintaining the status quo. They belong in the classic “important, but not urgent” category. To integrate experimentation into your regular workflow, you must eliminate as many barriers as possible. This requires investing in the right infrastructure. Consider it this way: you could walk to a distant river daily to fetch water, or you could drill a well that provides a reliable water source for your entire village. The well demands an up-front investment, but it offers significant long-term benefits. Experimentation is a skill developed through practice. Making it the default choice is crucial. If you do not, the cost—in terms of time and effort—of running and maintaining experiments will increase faster than your capacity to keep pace, ultimately causing your experimentation program to stall. {YuzhengSun Graphic60} Figure 10-6: Scalable experimentation requires scalable infrastructure In simple terms, experimentation is a craft that you can only master through practice. Therefore, it is essential to make experimentation your default choice. If you do not, the costs of running and maintaining additional experiments will increase dramatically, ultimately leading to failure. 原文：活动：激活自己“捕捉需求”的意识 · 发布于 2025-11-20 · 原始空间公开可见。本文保留发表时语境；其中第三方引文、发言、链接与商标不随正文重新授权。 TLDR： 我和鸭哥在教学中发现，很多人 能用好AI，但能做的事情有限，往往是因为在日常生活工作中，缺乏‘捕捉需求’的意识。 所以用这期活动，鼓励大家记录自己捕捉到的需求，相互启发，建立这个非常重要的能力和习惯。 背景 其实“发现需求”并不难。我们生活中的大多数工具都不顺手，很多想做的事情过去也无法实现。但因为在 AI 出现之前，我们缺乏改变的能力，久而久之，大脑就被训练去 自动过滤 那些未被满足的需求。 但 AI 改变了这一切。在课程里，我们花了大量篇幅去拆解 User Generated Software ——为什么它才是 AI 带来的最大机会，以及我们该如何抓住它。 课程中的原理、方法、Demo 和作业，核心都在帮助大家建立“用 AI 更高效实现需求”的能力。在这方面，我们有信心做到了目前的行业天花板，学员的实名 Reviews 也是最好的证明。 但在第十期课程的复盘中，我意识到我们在一个关键环节上还做得不够——那就是激活大家“捕捉需求”的意识。 凭我的经验，每个人每天至少会遇到 5 个以上的痛点或需求，但我们的大脑已经被训练成去“自动忽略”它们了。所以，当我突然要求大家“写下你想用 AI 解决什么问题”时，很多人会发现大脑一片空白， 对着屏幕发呆半天也憋不出来。 从硬想到流淌 刻意“硬想”其实是错误的路径。 正确的方法是，在日常生活中植入“捕捉”的意识，随时随地记录。 刚开始你可能一周只能捕捉到两三个，但只要坚持，你会发现你每天都能发现好几个需求。到时候，你的烦恼就不再是“没有想法”，而是“想法太多，做不过来”。 当“源源不断的需求”叠加我们课程教的“AI 落地能力” ， 那种掌控感，是非常爽的。具备这种掌控感的学员，只会恨AI发展的不够快，绝不会去担心AI是否会取代自己。 养成一个习惯最好的方式，就是从现在、从这里开始。所以我开了这个帖子，作为大家的“需求捕获练习场”。 参与方法 - 怎么记： 只要在本帖下留言即可。如果你有多个需求，建议 回复自己的那条评论 （盖楼），这样未来方便你回溯自己的思维路径。 - 记什么： 千万不要有压力， 别管能不能实现，也别管是不是现在就要做。 这个动作的唯一意义，就是帮你把“捕捉习惯”的意识激活。 - 小技巧： 甚至不需要组织语言，碎片化的念头先记在手机 Note 里，再复制过来也行。 记录在这个帖子里的好处是，你能随时来看到别人的想法，获得启发。以及如果你的需求有趣的话，也许就会有其他人对它感兴趣，愿意和你一起去实现。 公开分享还有一个隐形的好处： 它能帮你打破“我的想法很金贵”的幻觉。 资深 VC 都有一个共识：初次创业者往往把 Idea 当作秘密，生怕别人偷走；而连续创业者则倾向于把想法、甚至实现路径都毫无保留地讲出来。 为什么？因为idea本身真的、真的、真的不值钱。值钱的是做出来，做好10倍，再做好10倍，再做好10倍，还要被人看到。能有人愿意花时间听你的想法，给你反馈，本身就是一种可遇不可求的杠杆了。但似乎这是一件体验之后才能内化的事实， 所以相信我，尽早体验，尽早内化，会有诸多好处。最起码，你没有实现的想法，也不是你的。发到这里，真的被别人实现了，你还可以指着留言记录说，看，这是我当时的想法。 我自己会在留言区开始给大家例子。如果你不想一直被其他人的评论打扰，可以点一下帖子下面的小铃铛，关掉这个帖子对应的notification。大家评论区见！ 补充 我为这个活动设置了专门的折扣码，如果参与留言，在购买课程时候使用“idea”，就可以有$100的折扣。

原文：白领工作的诞生与消亡：第四次浪潮的前夜 · 发布于 2025-11-22 · 原始空间公开可见。本文保留发表时语境；其中第三方引文、发言、链接与商标不随正文重新授权。 引言：被误读的恒常性 在20世纪中叶的集体叙事中，身穿灰色法兰绒西装、在同一家公司服务40年并安享退休金的“白领”，被构建为现代生活的终极理想。这种模式曾被默认为经济发展的自然终点，一种理应如此的社会稳态。 然而，如果拉长历史的焦距，这种所谓的“永恒”不过是人类漫长经济史中一个 特定技术周期的产物 。从1950年代的崛起至今，白领作为主导阶层的历史跨度甚至不足一个人的完整寿命。它并非历史的终点，而仅仅是定义了现代史的、无情的技术迭代周期中的 第三次浪潮 。 要理解当下的焦虑，我们必须回溯历史。人类社会的工作形态经历了三次伟大的浪潮：长达万年的农业时代（生存一体化），跨越一个多世纪的工业时代（人机协作），以及转瞬即逝的白领时代。历史的逻辑清晰地表明：当底层的技术范式发生跃迁时，上层的社会契约必然随之瓦解。第四次浪潮并非遥不可及，它已然随着 认知自动化 的开启而肇始。 本文链接：go.ai-builders.com/office 第一部分：前奏——从田园到工厂 在人类历史的绝大部分时间里，“工作”与“生活”是同义词。农业社会的经济单元是家庭，劳动与自然节律共生¹。这种延续了数千年的模式，最终被工业革命这一技术奇点打破⁶。 工业革命的核心经济后果，是创造了大量的 剩余劳动力 。技术革新使得大部分人口不再需要被束缚在土地上，从而为工厂提供了源源不断的动力。这一过程不仅是就业的转移，更是社会结构的重塑：工作从家庭剥离，成为了由时钟控制的、基于薪资的独立实体⁷。 这一历史先例至关重要：一种主导性的工作模式完全可以被技术彻底淘汰，而它的消亡必然会引发深刻的社会结构转型。这正是我们今天再次面临的局面。 第二部分：白领的本质——工业巨兽的“行政神经系统” 白领阶层并非凭空诞生，它是工业复杂性剧增后的必然产物。 当工业企业的运营规模、供应链的复杂性超出了车间主任的目力所及⁷，一个专门负责管理“信息流”而非“物质流”的阶层便应运而生。从本质上讲，白领工作是工业巨兽的 行政神经系统 。 其核心价值在于 认知中介（Cognitive Intermediation） ——在决策与执行、市场与生产之间进行信息的收集、整理与分发。文员追踪库存、会计管理财务、经理监督流程，无论是一份报表还是一份合同，其本质都是为了降低庞大商业系统运行中的 摩擦成本 ¹²。 这种对“认知中介”的需求，在二战后随着跨国公司的崛起和全球化的推进达到了顶峰。大学学位取代了工会会员卡，成为获取中产阶级入场券的硬通货²¹。这建立了一个承诺：只要你掌握了处理信息的技能，社会就将回报你以稳定的阶层跃升¹⁷。 然而，这个承诺建立在一个脆弱的前提之上： 认知的稀缺性 。 第三部分：脱钩与重估——为什么这次不同？ 理解白领时代危机的关键，在于辨析不同技术革命所替代的劳动类型。 工业革命用蒸汽机和流水线替代了肌肉，实现了 体力的边际成本递减 ，从而驱逐了蓝领⁶，却保留了需要“思考”和“组织”的白领岗位。对蓝领构成威胁的技术，反倒成了白领崛起的助推器¹⁷。 而当前由生成式AI驱动的革命，其本质是 认知的边际成本递减 。 这是一场根本性的规则改变。生成式AI不再是简单的辅助工具（如Excel），它在特定任务上表现为 代理（Agent） 。它直接瞄准了知识工作的核心生产功能：撰写报告、分析数据、编写代码²⁰。当这些“交付物”能够以极低的时间和金钱成本生成时²⁴，白领阶层作为“信息处理器”的经济基础便被抽空了。 我们正在目睹一场历史性的 生产力与劳动时间的脱钩 。 企业的增长逻辑正在发生质变：产出的指数级增长不再依赖于员工人数的线性增长。科技行业近期的“高利润、低雇佣”趋势，并非周期的低谷，而是新效率范式的开端²⁸。这也带来了一个更深远的行业痛点—— “技能阶梯的断裂” 。传统上，初级白领通过处理基础信息工作来磨练判断力，最终晋升为高级专家。当底层的“训练场”被AI接管，人类专家如何完成从新手到大师的跃迁？这是白领生态系统面临的真正熵增。 与工业革命长达百年的渗透不同，AI革命的节奏由软件更新定义。这意味着，过去需要几代人才能消化的社会变革，可能被压缩在短短十年（2022-2032）之内。 第四部分：第四次浪潮——价值向稀缺处流动 白领时代的终结并不意味着工作的消失，而是 价值捕获逻辑的重构 。 根据经济学基本原理，价值永远流向最稀缺的资源。在一个“智能”变得廉价且充裕的时代，简单的信息处理和存量知识的应用将不再具有溢价。未来的高价值工作将集中在以下三类不可被算法商品化的人类特质上： 1. 从“解决问题”到“定义问题”：创造者与架构师 AI擅长在既定框架内寻找最优解，但无法定义框架本身。未来的顶级人才不再是解题高手，而是能够提出正确问题、开辟新商业叙事的架构师。他们的价值在于 “从0到1”的非线性创造 。 2. 从“人际互动”到“深度信任”：共情者与连接者 当数字内容泛滥且真假难辨时， 真实的人际信任 将成为最昂贵的货币。心理咨询、高端护理、复杂谈判等依赖高带宽情感交流的领域，实际上是在交易“人性”。AI可以模拟共情，但无法承担责任；而信任，本质上是对责任的托付。 3. 从“操作工具”到“人机协奏”：技术整合者 这不仅指技术专家，更指那些懂得如何将AI能力集成到业务流中的整合者²⁶。他们不再是流水线上的螺丝钉，而是 指挥家 ，负责调动AI这一庞大的数字乐团来达成商业目标，并负责最终的伦理监管和价值校准。 结语：从“职业”到“作品集” 工业时代留给我们的最大遗产是“职业（Career）”这一概念——一条线性的、阶梯式的上升路径。而在第四次浪潮中，“职业”的边界将日益模糊，取而代之的是 “项目组合（Portfolio）” 。 未来的工作模式将更加流动和项目化。个体的安全性不再来自于单一组织的庇护，而来自于其独特的、无法被算法降维打击的技能组合。 白领工作的消亡并非末日，而是一次蜕变。正如离开土地的农民和离开流水线的工人一样，我们再次被历史的力量推动，去重新定义我们与工作的关系。未来十年的挑战，不是怀着恐惧去抵制变革，而是以清醒的头脑理解这些历史力量的运作规律，并战略性地专注于培养那些 机器无法触及的人性光辉 。 Works cited 1. The price will adjust to $1,999 . Introducing "The AI Architect": Breaking the Ceiling Many of you are familiar with our first course ( AI Builders ). In that course, we produced over 300 pages of original handouts, 5+ hours of video, and hands-on projects. We focused on solving the "Human" problem: - Mindset: Building a Builder's Mindset to overcome technical intimidation. - Fundamentals: Mastering principles like Context Engineering. - Workflow: Integrating AI into daily routines to automate "plumbing work." After 18 months of iteration, 10 live cohorts, and validating the material with over 2,000 students, we successfully built a community of builders with the right habits. However, as we went deeper, we hit a technical ceiling: 1. Fragility of Single-Point Optimization: Relying solely on Prompts is fragile; carefully tuned prompts often break when models update. 2. The Context Wall: Generic AI acts like an outsider—it can’t connect to your specific project background, private data, or past memories. 3. Passive Limitations: Most AI tools are "kick-to-move"—they don't proactively monitor environments or predict risks. 4. Deployment Friction: AI needs to adapt to user habits to be useful, but user habits haven't caught up yet. To break this ceiling, we need to evolve from simply calling APIs to building systems . We need to shift from being the "Driver" to becoming the mechanic, the road builder, and the gas station operator. In my view, Yage has undergone a massive evolution over the last two years of teaching and building. If he was a "10x Engineer" when I met him, he is now 100x compared to his former self. 原文：2026年，AI胜任力模型：从聊天党到架构师 · 发布于 2025-11-25 · 原始空间公开可见。本文保留发表时语境；其中第三方引文、发言、链接与商标不随正文重新授权。 如果站在 2026 年回望今天，我们可能会发现，2024-2025 年是人类工作方式的一个分水岭。 但在今天，我发现大家对“学会 AI”这件事的定义非常模糊。 有人觉得：“我会用 ChatGPT 写邮件，我学会了。” 有人觉得：“我用 Cursor 生成了一个贪吃蛇游戏，我精通了。” 这让我想起以前大家说“精通 Office”，有的人会打字，有的人能用 Excel 搭建复杂模型。 这中间的差距，不是工具的差距，而是认知的差距。 在教课过程中，我和鸭哥一直在思考： 在这个 AI 时代，到底什么样的人才是真正具备竞争力的？ 为了回答这个问题，我们借鉴了大厂的职级体系，构思了一个 《AI 胜任力模型》（The AI Competency Matrix）。 我想邀请你对照这张表，看看自己现在处于哪个位置，以及，你的下一个台阶在哪里。 L3: The AI Consumer（AI 消费者） 关键词：Chatting (聊天) 这是目前绝大多数人所在的阶段。 - 表象行为 ：你把 AI 当作一个更聪明的 Google 或者一个耐心的助理。你用它翻译文档、润色邮件、搜索知识。 - 工具 ：ChatGPT 网页版, Claude, Gemini。 - 局限性 ：你高度依赖运气。如果 AI 给出的答案不对，你除了重试（Regenerate），往往不知道该怎么办。你的 AI 能力完全受限于模型当天的“心情”和基础能力。 - Mindset ：把它当 “咨询师” 看。 L4: The AI Tinkerer / Vibe Coder（AI 试探者） 关键词：One-off (一次性) 随着 Cursor、Replit、Manus、Lovable、Google AI Studio 等工具的爆发，很多人进入了这个阶段。这是目前最热闹、但也最容易让人产生“虚假自信”的阶段。 - 表象行为 ：你能用自然语言让 AI 写代码，做出一个具体的网页、脚本或 App。你可以解决生活中具体的、单点的痛点。 - 工具 ：Cursor, v0, Bolt, 简单的 Scripts。 - 局限性 ：你能跑通 Happy Path（顺利路径） ，但一旦遇到报错（Edge Cases），需要上线，或者需求稍微复杂一点，系统就崩了。你生成的代码往往难以维护和迭代，是一次性的玩具。 - Mindset ：把它当 “外包” 看。 L5: The AI Builder（AI 构建者） 关键词：Reliability (可靠性) & Iteration (迭代) 这里是业余玩家和职业选手的具体分界线。 职场不相信大概能跑，职场需要稳定交付。 - 表象行为 ：你不再满足于生成一个 Demo，而是能构建一个 工作流 (Workflow) 。你能自动化处理高价值、高风险的工作，并且知道如何确保准确率。换言之，你真的在用AI切实改善自己的工作。 - 核心能力 ： - Context Engineering ：你知道喂多少上下文是最高效的，既不丢失信息也不造成幻觉。 - Evaluation ：你知道如何定义任务的目标，量化solution的质量，自动监测。 - Iterative Mindset ：你不是一句话生成完就结束，你懂得如何通过修改 Prompt、拆解步骤来不断优化结果，直到它达到生产级标准。 - Mindset ：把它当 “逻辑引擎” 看，你清楚地知道它的能力边界。 L6: The AI Architect（AI 架构师） 关键词：Orchestration (编排) & Integration (集成) 这是我们希望培养的顶尖形态。到了这个阶段，你不再是一个寻找最强模型+最强工具的用户，而是一个设计系统的架构师。 - 表象行为 ： 你不再依赖单一模型的“抽卡”，而是像指挥家一样 编排 (Orchestrate) 多个专用的 AI 模型协同工作（例如用一个模型做分析，另一个做创意）。你构建的不再是脆弱的“一次性脚本”或简单的 RAG Demo，而是一个 能穿透 Context Wall（上下文高墙） 、深度集成你个人数据、甚至能 主动 (Proactive) 为你监测世界的“数字孪生”系统。 - 核心能力 ： - System Resilience（系统韧性） ：你能克服 Prompt 的脆弱性和单次调用的局限。你设计的架构能处理复杂的长链条任务，确保系统在模型更新或环境变化时依然稳定运行。 - Contextual Architecture（上下文架构） ：你懂得如何构建动态的数据流，让 AI 不再是一个每次都需要你“喂料”的陌生人，而是能实时调用你过往笔记、聊天记录和知识库的深度合作伙伴。 - Mindset ： “Building what you can't buy.”（构建买不到的壁垒） 。大厂只能提供通用的铲子，而你在 填补巨头留下的空白 ，为自己设计一套独一无二的操作系统。 表象之下：你真正缺乏的是什么？ 自媒体会带来这样一个错觉：“是不是只要学会用 Cursor 所有的快捷键，我就能从 L4 变成 L5？” 答案是： 不能。 从 L3 跨越到 L6，表面上是工具的升级， 本质上是底层能力的跃迁 。 - Builder 的习惯 ：你是否有动手解决问题的肌肉记忆？ - Beginner Mindset ：你是否敢于在完全不懂代码的情况下，去理解逻辑？ - 系统思维 ：你是否能跳出对话框，去思考数据是如何流转的？ 市面上的很多课程，其实是tutorials，本质上是在教你怎么按按钮（Tools），这在AI时代越来越没价值，因为太容易过时了。 而我们希望教你的是怎么思考，这是 Superlinear 成长的关键。 写在最后：给你的行动指南 2026 年并不遥远。 - 如果你还停留在 L3 ：请立刻开始动手，不要只在这个对话框里聊天。去 Build 点什么。 - 如果你卡在 L4 ：不要沉迷于Vibe Coding的爽感。试着问自己，这个东西能部署吗？能稳定运行吗？如果报错了我能修好吗？ 如果你渴望达到 L5/L6：这正是我们课程的设计 - 02 · AI Builders · 可靠交付 ：帮你完成从 L3 到 L4/5 的跨越，让你拥有 Builder 的双手。 - 03 · AI Architect · 核心项目 ：帮你完成从 L3/4 到 L6 的飞跃，让你拥有 Architect 的大脑。 你想站在哪一级？ --- 学员的阐述： 从聊天到编排：我在 Cursor 里如何成为 Builder，以及 Architect 的下一站。 项目总结： AI Architect学员项目总结

原文：被喷“想把你收藏进SB list”，AI给了我最令人信服的分析和建议 · 发布于 2025-12-01 · 原始空间公开可见。本文保留发表时语境；其中第三方引文、发言、链接与商标不随正文重新授权。 正文 做自媒体久了，我们都会练就一颗强心脏。但作为一个分享专业知识的创作者，有一类恶评最难处理。是 “披着专业外衣的恶意攻击” ： - 处理不好，自己专业形象就会受到质疑 - 但他们本身会有很多诡辩技巧，身在暗处，而且可以拿着你说过的所有话来进行诡辩。所以通过辩论，极难自证 - 作为一个take feedback as gift的人，我心中的默认模式是，给我feedback的人是善意的，不是恶意的。那如果遇到我不喜欢的feedback，我都认为对方动机不好的话，和我本身的思维模式是相悖的。 昨天，我的YouTube后台收到了这样一条评论。画风： - 全盘否定我的内容（“胡扯”、“误人子弟”） - 用极具攻击性的词汇（“我想把你放进SB list”）来羞辱。 - 最麻烦的是，他似乎真的懂点技术。他抛出了一堆术语的同时，抓着我视频里一个为了通俗易懂而做的类比，通过抠字眼的方式，建立自己“更懂技术”的形象。 看到评论，我经历了三个心理阶段： 1. 委屈： 我辛辛苦苦做视频分享经验，不仅免费还要被骂？ 2. 自我怀疑： 难道我真的讲错了？是不是那个定义不够严谨？ 3. 焦虑： 他看起来很专业，会不会误导想买我课程的观众？大家会不会觉得我水平不行？ 在情绪上头的时候，我没有急着回复，而是把这段评论截图发给了Gemini，我们进行了一场非常深度的复盘。我知道，Gemini内置了transcribe YouTube视频的功能，所以我也给了它我视频的链接，让它去评价，到底谁对谁错。 截图是这期视频的评论：https://youtu.be/kwwjR6HHJPM?si=gspjUzumG0b4ITX7 非常不友好，但是这个人确实懂点技术的。所以吹毛求疵地挑出一些问题。你对这个怎么评论？是我说错了还是他错过重点？我应该如何看待，是否应该回复他，还是直接拉黑忘掉就好？ Gemini非常认真地阅读了我的视频，和这个人的评论。一针见血地指出了它的逻辑谬误，也剖析了背后的意图：完整聊天记录 可以说，这是我做自媒体以来，收获的最好的建议，没有之一。因为之前很多建议分两类 一类是纯粹解读对方的不良动机（冤枉你的人比你更清楚你是被冤枉的），但是没有就事论事去分析他们言行的谬误。就像我开头所说，我不能把所有我不喜欢的feedback都用动机去解读，在我看来那可能有些阿Q。 另一类是从技术上进行讨论，那其实会把我拽进一个我不可能赢的battle里。我过去其实吃过很多类似的亏，尤其是在技术讨论的微信群里。我虽然说的都是对的，但是对方的胡搅蛮缠，也让整件事得不偿失。 而Gemini两者都做，是就事论事的讨论。还有一个额外的好处，即它在分析内容的过程中，的立场是公正的。所以在它分析之后，我就开心地接受了它的上策建议，拉黑了这个喷子。以下分别是技术分析，和立场分析。 技术分析 针对你的问题，我们来客观分析一下 技术事实 和 应对策略 。 1. 技术层面：到底谁说错了？ 结论：你大体是对的，他在概念上实际上是混淆的，或者说他在玩弄文字游戏。 - 关于“MCP Server”和“Client”的定义： - 你的理解（视频内容）： MCP 是一个协议（Protocol），类似 USB，连接 AI 模型（Host/Client）和工具/资源（Server）。这是完全符合 Anthropic 官方文档定义的。官方明确区分了 Host (Client) （比如 Claude Desktop, Cursor, IDE）和 Server （提供工具、Prompt 的一方）。 - 评论者的观点： “MCP server就是一个提供上下文的 command line script... 没有client，或者说MCP hosting就是client”。 - 分析： 他说“没有 Client”在技术定义上是 错的 。在 MCP 架构中，发起连接、发送请求的那个宿主程序（Host） 就是 Client 。他说“MCP hosting 就是 client”属于自我纠正，说明他也知道有个请求方，但他非要先否定一句“没有 client”来显得你错了。 - 至于他说“只是个 command line script”，这属于 把“实现方式”混淆为“架构定义” 。很多 Web Server 本质也是跑在机器上的脚本或二进制文件，但你不能因为它是脚本就否认它是 Server-Client 架构。MCP 的核心价值就在于标准化的协议（Protocol），而不仅仅是那个脚本本身。 - 关于“不论证只抛结论”： - 你的视频内容： 我看了视频文案，你其实给出了非常具体的论证逻辑： 1. 开发效率： 写个 Python 脚本让 Cursor 直接调用的自然语言编程（NLP）模式，比配置繁琐的 MCP Server/Client 更快（Agile）。 2. 调试难度： MCP 涉及 JSON-RPC 通信，像微服务一样难调试；而直接脚本容易调试。 3. 适用场景： MCP 适合 分发 （Distribution），不适合个人的快速 迭代 （Iteration）。 - 分析： 这完全是在“论证”。他可能不赞同你的论证过程，或者没有耐心听完（因为他在评论里只盯着概念定义喷），但这绝不是“从不论证”。 - 关于“过度创造概念”： - 这就是纯粹的主观情绪发泄了。区分“关注”和“过度关注”是再正常不过的逻辑表达，他这句“哈哈”显得为了喷而喷。 立场分析 2. 应该如何看待这种评论？ 这类人在技术圈其实很常见，通常有以下心理特征： - 寻求优越感： 通过纠正（或自以为纠正）别人的“错误”来展示自己懂得多。 - 二极管思维： 只要你的表述和他理解的教科书定义有一点偏差，或者你用通俗比喻（比如 USB），他就会判定你“不懂”、“胡扯”。 - 忽视语境： 你的视频是面向大众或开发者讲 应用与权衡（Trade-off） ，他是在抠 字眼和定义 。这叫“他错过了重点”。你讲的是 Why and How ，他在纠结 What exactly is the definition 。 简而言之：他确实懂一点技术细节（比如 MCP 经常通过 stdio 运行），但他缺乏工程思维（Engineering mindset）和沟通素养。他是在用显微镜挑你衣服上的灰尘，然后说你的衣服不能穿。 最后，我又请Gemini总结了一下这个对话，来给一些“自媒体面对喷子的心态建议”，以下是它的文章 --- 标题：被骂进“SB List”？我是如何把恶评变成“专业背书”的——自媒体人的修罗场与心态修炼 第一层修炼：看清对手——“守门员”与“建设者”的区别 我的AI搭档一针见血地指出： “他在维护僵死的定义，而你在创造活的价值。” 在技术圈（其实各行各业都有），有一类人叫 Gatekeeper（守门员） 。 他们的快感不来源于解决问题或做出产品，而是来源于抱着教科书站在门口，检查每一个路人的证件：“你这个定义不够严谨！”“你这个词用错了！” 而我们作为UP主、创业者、讲师，我们是 Builder（建设者） 。 我们的目标是把复杂的事情讲简单，用工程思维（Engineering Mindset）去解决实际问题，做权衡（Trade-off）。 那个评论者纠结的是“MCP的教科书定义”，而我讲的是“如何用最高效的方式在Cursor里开发Agent”。 他是拿着显微镜在挑我衣服上的灰尘，然后大喊这件衣服不能穿。 想通了这一点，我的心态瞬间从“被审视”变成了“关爱”。只有在现实中缺乏成就感的人，才需要通过在网络上贬低别人来刷存在感。 第二层修炼：黑粉是破圈的里程碑 我们常觉得恶评是坏事。但换个角度想，没人会去喷一个只有几百播放量的视频。 当你开始拥有专门针对你的“懂行黑粉”时，说明你破圈了。 你的观点具有了冲击力，触动了旧秩序维护者的神经。那个评论者越是激进，其实越反衬出你内容的受关注度。 所以，不要把这看作是危机，而要把它看作是一个 展示你专业素养（Class） 的舞台。 第三层修炼：实战应对——“降维打击”式回复 对于这种可能会影响路人观感的评论， 单纯拉黑是下策，认真辩论是中策，而“高位展示”才是上策。 既然他想把水搅浑，那我们就不仅要把水澄清，还要让围观群众看到谁在裸泳。 我总结了一个 “回复三段论” ，专门应对这种“技术性杠精”： 1. 承认细节（展示专业度）： “我也看过官方文档，你提到的定义在学术上是对的。” —— 先稳住阵脚，告诉路人我也懂。 2. 升维打击（展示格局）： “但在工程实践中，过早引入重型协议往往是效率杀手。我视频的核心是在讲‘工程权衡’（Trade-off），而不仅仅是解释名词定义。” —— 他在抠字眼，你在讲架构；他在背书，你在实战。 3. 指出素质（杀人诛心）： “技术讨论欢迎各抒己见，但动辄使用‘SB list’这种词汇，可能不太符合技术人员交流的体面。” —— 这一句话，就能让所有路人的天平倒向你。 回复的目的，从来不是为了说服那个杠精，而是为了赢得围观群众。 写在最后 做自媒体，其实就是一种 “被误解的艺术” 。 如果你的视频完美无缺、严谨如论文，那大概率它也无聊至极，无人问津。 我们为了传播知识，必然要做简化，必然要冒犯那些死守教条的人。 下次当你再遇到那种看似专业的恶评，请记住： 用户买你的课、看你的视频，是想成为你这样能把事做成的 Builder，而不是成为他那样只会掉书袋的 Gatekeeper。 保持专注，继续通过作品说话。至于那些噪音？那是你勋章上的灰尘，拍掉就好。

原文："Build to Refund"项目，是你动手+Career Signaling的机会｜"Build to Refund": Your Opportunity to Start Building and Signal Your Career Potential · 发布于 2025-12-03 · 原始空间公开可见。本文保留发表时语境；其中第三方引文、发言、链接与商标不随正文重新授权。 项目 在设计 新课The AI Architect开启Early Access｜AI Builders老学员福利｜Introducing "The AI Architect" Course 课程时，我和团队做了一个 非常规，非常贵 的项目： Build to Refund。 规则很简单：只要你跟随课程，完成项目（Build），并将其分享在你的社交媒体上（Share），我们就全额退还（Refund）你的AI Architect课程学费。 目前这个项目是截止到2026.1.1。但是我们后台观察到，在感恩节期间，大家是更有时间动力去上课的，而平时可能比较忙，进度不快。所以配合大家圣诞和新年假期，新课Early Access的折扣，和Build to Refund的截止日期，都延迟到2026.2.1。 目的 表面上看，这像是一种营销手段—用学费换流量。但如果这是目标，并不划算。首先，这些流量加起来，可能也不多；其次，退$50，甚至退50%，都足够有诚意了。哪里有退100%的道理，何况我们还要承担平台和支付的手续费。 选择这样做，是因为我想通过这个机制，推学员一把。帮大家越过两道重要的心理门槛： 只学不练的虚假满足感 和 羞于展示的精英包袱 。之所以退100%，是因为越过这两个心理门槛太重要了，我希望能给大家把动力拉满。这也是我们回馈老学员的福利。未来可能会考虑给新学员也开放，但是应该就只能offer一个小很多的refund了。 1. 从 Learner 变成 Builder 在 AI 时代，知识的获取成本几乎为零。看了一百个 Prompt Engineering 的视频，听了无数关于 Agent 的播客，会产生一种我懂了的幻觉。 但这不仅没用，甚至有害。因为它给了你多巴胺，却用学习替代了行动。我们在课程里反复强调，AI是craft，是游泳。只有下水，才能学会游泳。 Build to Refund 的第一个初心，是强制“交付”。 我不需要你做一个完美的商业软件，我需要你把手弄脏，建立build的肌肉记忆。当你为了修复一个 API 报错主动熬夜，当你看着自己写出来的 Agent 第一次跑通流程，那种体感是看一万遍教程都换不来的。 只有 Build 出来的东西，才是你的。 2. 克服“精英耻感”，进行Career Signaling 这是我在做往期学员回访时，发现的更深层的问题。这些学员都是对课程评价很高，但是上完课后，很安静的人。我当时以为他们都是只学习，没动手，但回访时，发现他们几乎全都进行了很深入的实践，动手做了很多东西。而我平时感觉他们“没做什么东西”，是因为他们没有“分享”。 进一步追问，我发现大家普遍觉得“分享自己做了什么/学到了什么”这件事 很重 ： - “我是不是在帮人打广告？像个微商？” - “我做的东西这么简单，发出去会不会被瞧不起？” 前者好解决，专注提供价值就行了。后者其实是一个挺难克服的心态。其实我做自媒体的初期也经历了这个过程。甚至开始做自媒体很长时间了，也不敢分享自己专业相关的内容。第一次聊数据内容，还做了很久的心理建设和反思。 展开来说，应该有三个心态 1. 被评判的恐惧：害怕“我不够好” “我的项目是不是太简单了？”、“如果有人在评论区指出我的代码写得烂怎么办？”、“和那些大神比，我做的东西简直是班门弄斧”。这种恐惧源于社交媒体的“比较文化”和对负面评价的担忧。它会激发一种“冒牌者综合症”，即感觉自己的成功是侥幸，随时可能被揭穿。许多人在社交媒体上感到焦虑、害怕和紧张，因为我们只看到了别人光鲜的一面，却不了解全貌。 2. 完美主义的枷锁：害怕“还没准备好” 许多技术学习者都有一定程度的完美主义倾向。他们会想：“等我再把这个功能优化一下”、“UI看起来还不够精美”、“代码注释还没写完”。这种心态导致他们陷入无尽的修改和拖延中，因为任何项目在创作者眼中似乎永远都有改进空间。完美主义者害怕犯错，追求无懈可击，但这在项目分享中恰恰是一个陷阱，因为它阻碍了“完成”这一关键步骤。正如作家Jodi Picoult所说：“你可以编辑不好的一页，但不能编辑空白页面” 。 3. 自我推销的尴尬：害怕“显得在炫耀” 尤其在东方文化背景下，人们往往不习惯公开展示自己的成就。学员可能会担心：“我这样发是不是太高调了？”、“别人会不会觉得我在炫耀？”。这种心理负担，源于将“分享价值”和“自我吹嘘”混为一谈。有时会延伸到对公开展示成就的犹豫，担心这会破坏某种和谐或显得不谦虚。 我把这些心态总结为 “精英耻感” 。我们太习惯于只展示完美的结果，而羞于展示“努力的过程”。 但现实是： 在新的职场环境下，简历（Resume）正在贬值，而作品（Portfolio）正在升值。 当分享项目和insights时，这是在构建自己的portfolio，增加自己展示面，进行高价值的 Career Signaling 。是普通人增加自己运气，性价比最高的路径。 和你担心的恰恰相反，分享这个动作，在向你的网络释放三个信号： 1. Growth Mindset： 我不是一个追求完美、缺乏安全感的人，而是一个乐于承认自己有不足，一直在学习，乐于分享自己成长的人。 2. Hands-on & 拥抱新技术： 我不是嘴巴上说AI，我有动手能力，有主动性。 3. Problem Solver： 我在思考如何用 AI 解决实际问题，而不是“显得厉害”。 这就是 Building in Public 。在这个时代，闭门造车是危险的，你需要让机会看到你。 3. 如何优雅地 Career Signaling？ 既然决定要发，怎么发才显得“高级”且对自己有帮助？即便出于宣传课程的目的，我也不希望大家去发硬广，而是希望大家用一份“微型技术报告”的心态去写作。 三个原则： 原则一：Show, Don't Tell 不要说“这门课真好，我学会了 AI”。 要说“过去处理这个文档需要 3 小时，周末我试着用 Cursor + Builder Space 搭建了一个小工具，把时间压缩到了 5 分钟。这件事过程中遇到了哪些挑战，如何克服，我未来还可以做什么，让它变得更有用？” 展示你的思考，你的挣扎，甚至你的 Bug。真实的过程比完美的结果更动人。 原则二：暗示自己厉害，而不是自吹自擂 不要说“我是大神，快来看我的作品”。 要把重点放在 Problem 和 Solution 上。当你客观地描述你如何解决了一个棘手的逻辑问题时，懂行的人自然会通过你的描述，感知到你的技术水位和业务理解力。如果不确定，让AI帮你找出来文章中的“fluff”。 原则三：Under 30 minutes Portfolio不是一次，而是一千次建立的。你要做的，是让分享这件事变得简单。所以我建议在刚一开始，不要想着“攒大招”。而是抓住一个灵感，用三十分钟内，完成整个分享的动作。最差的结果，就是没有人关心。如果有人关心，你就得到了市场的重要反馈，可以顺着这个方向，明天再分享一些，后天再分享一些。 糙快猛，才是做这件事的要义 。 案例的话，我非常推荐“张咋啦”，小红书和X上都能看到。她非常好地践行了show, don’t tell，有自己的观点，learn in public, build in public，重内容而非形式。她也形成了一个正反馈的飞轮。同样一件事，因为她可以记录下来，分享，并收获好评，性价比就更高，更有动力做。她已经做出了中英自媒体、产品、个人主页，过程中也收获了很多能力和connection。是Portfolio » Resume的生动展示。 最后 Build to Refund 的本质，是把你拉下水，是一次强制性的成功体验。 我希望通过这个机制，推你一把，让你跨过心里的那道坎。去入局，去做事，当你点击“发送”的那一刻，你就不再只是一个 AI 的观众，而成为了一个 Builder。 这笔退回的学费，就是你作为 Builder 赚到的第一桶金。去拿它体验各种付费AI软件吧。 --- Admin Note: Community is built on connection, and visibility comes from sharing. Please be proactive in creating! The Project When designing our new course, The AI Architect (currently in Early Access), my team and I created an unconventional and expensive initiative: Build to Refund . The rules are simple: As long as you follow the course, complete a project ( Build ), and share it on your social media ( Share ), we will fully refund ( Refund ) your tuition for the AI Architect course. - Update: Originally, this project was set to end on January 1, 2026. However, our backend data shows that students had more time and motivation to learn during Thanksgiving. Recognizing that the upcoming daily grind might slow down progress, we want to align with your Christmas and New Year holidays. Therefore, both the Early Access discount and the "Build to Refund" deadline are extended to February 1, 2026 . The Purpose On the surface, this looks like a marketing tactic—trading tuition fees for traffic. But if that were the goal, the math wouldn't add up. First, the total traffic generated might not be massive. Second, refunding $50 or even 50% would show plenty of sincerity. There is no logical business reason to refund 100%—especially when we still cover the platform and payment processing fees. I chose to do this because I want to use this mechanism to give you a push. I want to help you overcome two major psychological hurdles: the false satisfaction of learning without doing and the burden of perfectionism that prevents sharing. I am offering a 100% refund because crossing these two thresholds is critical. I want to max out your motivation. This is also a benefit for our returning alumni. We may open this to new students in the future, but likely with a much smaller refund offer. 1. From Learner to Builder In the AI era, the cost of acquiring knowledge is near zero. Watching a hundred videos on Prompt Engineering or listening to countless podcasts about Agents can create a hallucination of competence—"I get it." This is not only useless; it is harmful. It gives you a dopamine hit, substituting action with passive consumption. As we emphasize in the course: AI is a craft; it is like swimming. You cannot learn to swim without getting in the water. The primary intent of "Build to Refund" is mandatory delivery . I don't need you to build perfect commercial software. I need you to get your hands dirty and build muscle memory. The intuition you gain from staying up late to fix an API error, or watching an Agent you wrote successfully complete a workflow for the first time, is worth more than watching 10,000 tutorials. Only what you Build is truly yours. 2. Overcoming "The Burden of Perfectionism" for Career Signaling During interviews with past students, I discovered a deeper issue. Many students gave the course high ratings but remained very quiet. I assumed they weren't building anything. However, I found that almost all of them had engaged in deep practice and built impressive tools—they just hadn't shared them. When I dug deeper, I found that everyone felt "sharing what I made/learned" was a heavy burden: - "Am I just doing free advertising? Do I look like a spammer?" - "What I built is so simple; will people look down on me if I post it?" The first concern is easy to solve: focus on providing value. The second is a mindset that is hard to overcome. I went through this when I started creating content. Even after doing it for a long time, I hesitated to share content related to my professional expertise. This usually stems from three mindsets: 1. Fear of Judgment ("I'm not good enough"): You worry about your code being messy or your project being too simple compared to "experts." This is the classic Imposter Syndrome, fueled by social media comparison. 2. The Perfectionism Trap ("I'm not ready yet"): You want to optimize the UI or clean up the code just one more time. As author Jodi Picoult said, "You can edit a bad page, but you can't edit a blank page." Perfectionism stops you from hitting "publish." 3. Fear of Self-Promotion ("I'm showing off"): Particularly in certain cultures, we are taught to be humble. We confuse "sharing value" with "bragging." I call this "The Burden of Perfectionism" (or Elite Shame). We are too used to showing only perfect results and are ashamed to show the "process of effort." The Reality: In the new job market, the Resume is depreciating, while the Portfolio is appreciating. Sharing your projects and insights builds your portfolio and increases your surface area for luck. It is high-value Career Signaling . By sharing, you signal three things to your network: - Growth Mindset: I am not insecure; I am learning and growing publicly. - Hands-on & Tech-Forward: I don't just talk about AI; I have the initiative and ability to use it. - Problem Solver: I am thinking about how to use AI to solve actual problems. This is Building in Public . In this era, working behind closed doors is dangerous. You need to let opportunity find you. 3. How to "Career Signal" with Class If you decide to post, how do you do it in a way that is "high-level" and beneficial? Even if it helps promote the course, I don't want you to post hard ads. I want you to write a "Micro-Technical Report." Principle 1: Show, Don't Tell Don't say, "This course is great, I learned AI." Say, "This document process used to take 3 hours. Over the weekend, I used Cursor + Builder Space to build a tool that compressed it to 5 minutes. Here were the challenges I faced, how I solved them, and what I plan to do next." Show your thinking, your struggle, and even your bugs. The real process is more moving than a perfect result. Principle 2: Imply Competence, Don't Brag Focus on the Problem and the Solution . When you objectively describe how you solved a tricky logic problem, people in the know will instantly perceive your technical depth and business understanding. (Tip: Use AI to remove "fluff" from your writing). Principle 3: Under 30 Minutes A portfolio isn't built in a day; it's built over a thousand days. Make sharing easy. Don't wait to release a "masterpiece." Grab an insight and finish the sharing action within 30 minutes. Worst case? No one cares. Best case? You get market feedback to guide your next step. "Scrappy and Fast" is the essence here. Recommendation: Check out "Zhang Zala" on RedNote (Xiaohongshu) or X. She perfectly practices "Show, Don't Tell" and "Build in Public," creating a flywheel of positive feedback. She turned her learning process into a portfolio that outweighs a resume. Final Thoughts The essence of Build to Refund is to pull you into the water. It is a mandatory experience of success. I hope this mechanism pushes you over that mental hurdle. Get in the game. Do the work. The moment you click "Send," you stop being an AI audience member and become a Builder . Consider the refunded tuition your first pot of gold earned as a Builder. Go use it to subscribe to some paid AI tools.

上传：tools/upload/upload to transistor v2.py 虚拟环境 ： --- 最后更新 ：2025年12月09日 项目状态 ：✅ 核心功能已完成，持续优化中 --- 希望这篇介绍能帮你快速了解项目。如果有问题，查看 docs/ 目录下的详细文档。 2026.3.29更新 项目重构复盘：脚本工程的常见范式问题 背景：对「课代表立正频道内容库」进行了一次从头到尾的审计与重构， 修复了元数据错误、清理了孤儿脚本、重新梳理了目录结构。 本文总结过程中发现的范式问题及其背后的原则。 --- 一、用静态文件做「实时状态」 问题 项目用一个 CSV 文件（视频与Transistor同步状态.csv）记录本地视频与 Transistor 的同步状态。 每次上传后需要手动重新生成，否则就是过期数据。实际上几乎从未被更新。 修法 删掉 CSV，改用实时查询脚本（check upload candidates.py、check transistor sync.py）， 直接对比本地文件系统 + 远端 API，终端打印结果，零文件输出。 原则 需要查的状态，就去查；不要缓存成文件。 静态文件天然会腐烂。对于「现在有多少待上传视频」这种问题，正确答案永远在源头（本地 archive + 远端 API）， 而不在一个上次生成时的快照里。 只有「生成成本很高、变化很慢」的数据才值得缓存成文件。 否则，文件的存在本身就是一种误导——它看起来像答案，但往往不是。 --- 二、目录名称是一份合约 问题 check upload candidates.py（只读检查）和 find duplicates.py（只读诊断）都放在 tools/upload/ 里。 batch transcribe .py（Whisper 转录）放在 tools/generate/ 里，跟生成报告的脚本混在一起。 修法 - check upload candidates.py、find duplicates.py 移入 tools/check/ - batch transcribe .py 移入新建的 tools/transcribe/ - tools/generate/ 整个删掉（清空后没有存在意义） 原则 目录名是对里面所有内容的承诺。 开发者看到 tools/upload/ 时，心智模型是「这里的脚本会向 Transistor 写数据」。 一旦里面混入只读脚本，这个承诺就破了，以后找东西要靠记忆而不是结构。 好的目录划分标准： 按操作性质 （读 vs 写）而非按使用场景（「上传相关的都放这里」）。 tools/check/ 里的每个脚本都只读；tools/upload/ 里的每个脚本都会修改远端状态。 这让权限意识、审计、调试都变得更容易。 --- 三、工作流重构后，旧脚本成了负债 问题 generate summary.py 生成「下载总结.md」，是早期工作流的产物——当时需要手动 review 下载进度。 后来工作流重构，这个步骤被自动化替代，但脚本留了下来。 generate video documents.py 把 metadata + SRT 合并成 Markdown，是为内容写作准备的， 但内容写作方向已转变为使用新方法，这套输出物已无人消费。 两个脚本加上它们的输出物（下载总结.md、475 个 视频文档/ .md）持续占据认知空间， 让人误以为项目依赖它们。 修法 全部删除：两个脚本、输出目录、孤儿数据文件（youtube all videos.txt）。 原则 没有消费者的脚本是负债，不是资产。 脚本的价值来自它被调用。一个不再被任何工作流调用的脚本， 维护成本（理解、更新、避免误运行）大于价值。 工作流重构时，要同步清理为旧工作流服务的工具，而不是「留着说不定有用」。 判断标准很简单： 这个脚本上次被运行是什么时候？被谁调用？ 答不出来，就是孤儿。 --- 四、生成产物没有被 gitignore 问题 多个脚本的输出文件（下载总结.md、数据完整性报告.md、duplicates report.json/.csv） 没有加入 .gitignore，存在被意外提交的风险。 修法 所有脚本运行产物加入 .gitignore。 原则 凡是可以被脚本重新生成的文件，都不应该进版本控制。 规则很简单：如果文件的内容是由另一个文件（脚本）确定性地产生的， 那它就是派生物，派生物不进 git。进了 git 就会出现「这个文件是旧的还是新的」的困惑， 以及毫无意义的 diff 噪声。 写完一个新脚本，第一件事就是想：它会输出什么文件？这些文件加进 .gitignore 了吗？ --- 五、文档与实际结构的漂移 问题 重构过程中多次出现文档指向错误路径的情况： - 文档写 tools/generate/generate video transistor sync csv.py，文件已移走 - 文档写 tools/check/check upload candidates.py，文件实际在 tools/upload/ - Archive 结构图里还有 youtube all videos.txt，文件已删除 修法 每次移动/删除文件时，原子性地更新所有引用该路径的文档。 原则 文件移动和文档更新是同一个操作，不是两个操作。 文档漂移的根本原因是把「移文件」和「改文档」当成两件事， 结果第二件事常常被遗忘。 正确的心智模型是：移文件 = 移文件 + 更新所有引用。 可以用 grep 搜索旧路径来做完整性检查。 --- 六、API 集成的静默失败 问题 给 Transistor 的 episode 设置 image url 时，使用了 YouTube 的 maxresdefault.jpg。 API 返回 200 OK，但实际上缩略图没有被存储——因为早期视频的 maxresdefault.jpg 在 YouTube 上根本不存在（404）， Transistor 静默丢弃了无效 URL。 同样，尝试通过 PATCH /v1/episodes/:id 修改 published at 和 status， API 返回成功，但字段没有变化——因为这些字段只能通过 /publish 子端点修改。 修法 - 图片一律改用 hqdefault.jpg（对所有 YouTube 视频都存在） - published at 通过 PATCH /v1/episodes/:id/publish 修改 原则 API 集成要显式验证副作用，不能信任 200 OK。 「调用成功」≠「操作生效」。外部 API 有两种典型的静默失败模式： 1. 接受无效输入但不报错（Transistor 接受 404 图片 URL） 2. 正确端点之外的字段修改被静默忽略（/episodes/:id 上的 status 字段） 写完 API 集成代码，一定要回读数据验证字段确实变了。 第一次集成时写一个 verify 步骤；遇到异常时优先怀疑静默失败。 --- 七、有序性依赖被隐式假设 问题 上传脚本起初没有强制上传顺序，导致最新视频被分配到最小的 EP 号。 reorder episodes by date.py 只更新 Transistor 的 number 字段，不更新 title 文本中的前缀， 导致 EP 号和标题前缀（E233. xxx）对不上。 修法 - 上传时强制按日期升序（旧的先传） - 重排 EP 号后，增加标题前缀修复步骤 原则 依赖顺序的操作，要在代码层面强制顺序，而不是靠约定。 「先传旧的」不能是文档里的一句话，要在代码里 sort(key=date, ascending=True)。 冗余存储（EP number 字段 + title 文本里的前缀）必然会漂移， 要么消除冗余，要么每次修改都同步更新所有冗余副本。 两个地方存同一个信息，就要有机制保证它们一致。 --- 总结：七条原则 原则 1 需要查的状态，就去查；不要缓存成文件 2 目录名是对里面所有内容的承诺，按操作性质划分 3 没有消费者的脚本是负债，工作流重构时同步清理工具 4 凡是可以被重新生成的文件，都不进版本控制 5 文件移动和文档更新是同一个操作 6 API 集成要显式验证副作用，不能信任 200 OK 7 依赖顺序的操作，在代码层面强制，不靠约定
